key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow makes it possible to map thermodynamic stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions, revealing that stable regions are narrow and concentrated at high iodide content.
engineering_relevance: The results directly inform compositional design for more stable perovskite solar absorbers, especially by showing that Sn-based alloys offer less stability headroom than Pb-based ones.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials were trained on DFT data to accelerate structure relaxations.
Secondary ML models predicted energies from unrelaxed structures to make quaternary alloy screening tractable.
Free-energy landscapes were computed across composition and phase space, including alloy disorder and FA orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to evaluate free-energy landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3 across compositions, comparing stability trends between Pb- and Sn-based systems.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on ML models trained on DFT data, extrapolation outside the sampled composition/structure space may reduce reliability.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
